description: We are a team of High School students passionate about space, AI, Earth science, and technology. Our team combines experience in Python, research, data analysis, and problem-solving, and we're excited to apply these skills to a real-world challenge through NASA Space Apps. We value teamwork, creativity, and continuous learning, and we're looking forward to collaborating, sharing ideas, and building an impactful project together while enjoying the hackathon experience.
summary:
Earth science is an interactive platform designed to explore and analyze the earth science data easier. The main goal is to allowing users to investigate environmental changes through asking simple questions in natural language like: "Is drought increase in California?" or "Is my city getting hotter?". The platform uses AI to analyze and identify the relevant scientific data from resources such ass NASA satellite missions and Google Earth Engine. The collected data is presented through maps, graphs, and comparisons. Based on the statistical analysis, the platform identifies trends and measure the extent of these changes. 
Finally, Earth detective provides a clear summary of findings explain changing, where, and how significant the changes are.
details: 1. How Does the Project Work? TerraSleuth is designed to make exploring environmental changes easier for everyone. Instead of having to search through complicated scientific datasets, users can simply ask questions in natural language, such as "Is drought getting worse in California?" The platform then identifies what environmental factor they are asking about and which geographical area they want to investigate. 2. Understanding the User's Question When a user enters a question, TerraSleuth uses a Question Translator to understand what they are looking for. It identifies the environmental variable and location mentioned in the question, then matches them with the appropriate datasets. At this stage, the system uses predefined keywords and supported options to make sure the selected data is relevant to the investigation. 3. Data Collection Once the question is understood, TerraSleuth collects the required environmental data using Google Earth Engine (GEE). It works with several Earth observation datasets, each providing different types of information: - NASA GPM: Provides precipitation data. - MODIS: Provides vegetation and land surface temperature data. - GLDAS: Provides soil moisture and evapotranspiration data. - MERRA-2: Provides atmospheric and climate data. By using these sources, the platform can examine environmental conditions over different periods and identify how they have changed over time. 4. Data Processing and Statistical Analysis After collecting the data, TerraSleuth processes it and organizes it into time-series data to make environmental patterns easier to understand. It also applies statistical methods to investigate whether the observed changes represent actual trends: - Mann-Kendall Test: Determines whether a variable has an increasing or decreasing trend and checks its statistical significance. - Sen's Slope Estimator: Measures how quickly the variable is changing over time. - Ordinary Least Squares (OLS): Estimates the overall linear trend in the collected data. Using these methods together helps the platform provide a clearer understanding of environmental changes rather than relying only on visual observations. 5. Results and Visualization The final results are displayed through an interactive interface built with Streamlit, while Plotly is used to create graphs and visualizations. Users can explore the collected data, examine important statistical values such as p-values and slopes, and view a simplified investigation verdict that explains whether the environmental variable is increasing, decreasing, or showing no significant trend. 6. Tools and Technologies TerraSleuth was developed using Python, Streamlit, Plotly, and Google Earth Engine. Each technology has a specific role in the platform, from accessing and processing scientific data to presenting the results in an interactive way. Ultimately, the idea behind TerraSleuth is to turn complex Earth science data into clear and understandable evidence, allowing more people to investigate environmental changes and make better sense of what is happening to our planet.
